Blaszki Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Błaszki, Poland

Demolished. Błaszki, founded in the 14th century, saw its first documented Jewish resident in 1717; the community grew substantially under the Lipscy family's mid-18th-century ownership, reaching 900 people by 1835 and 60% of the population by the 1860s. In early September 1939, Germans arrested and executed ten leading kehilla members at this cemetery; the remaining Jews were deported to General Government territory on December 20, 1939. This cemetery, confirmed to exist by 1830 under caretaker Jakób Huberman, was destroyed during WWII and its remaining tombstones stolen afterward; the site is now farmland with no visible remains. Its location, in the Wilczkowice administrative area about 2.5km from central Błaszki, is only presumed based on limited records.
